name: ZMA
lead: ZMA is a supplement combining zinc, magnesium and vitamin B6, taken before bed by lifters, bodybuilders and other athletes. People use it to support deeper sleep and recovery and to maintain testosterone, with the aim of training harder and building more muscle over time. It was developed by Victor Conte, founder of BALCO Laboratories; the standard formulation contains zinc monomethionine aspartate, magnesium aspartate and pyridoxine (vitamin B6) [1].

Published studies are few. A 1998 company-linked study reported strength gains in football players [1]. A 2009 trial in 14 exercising men found raised serum and urinary zinc but no significant change in total or free testosterone [2], and more recent trials have looked at sleep and next-morning performance [3][4].
On T Nation, members describe ZMA mostly as a sleep aid, with several reporting that they fall asleep more easily or sleep more deeply, and some noting they cannot tell whether it helps [5][6][7][8].
infobox: Zinc monomethionine aspartate, magnesium aspartate, vitamin B6 [1]

paras: The original product pairs 30 mg zinc, 450 mg magnesium and 10.5 mg vitamin B6 per serving, and the manufacturer advises taking it on an empty stomach 30 to 60 minutes before bed, avoiding calcium because of claimed absorption interference [1]. SNAC holds the trademark but the formula is not patented, so other brands sell similar products [1]. Variants include ZMA-5, which adds 5-HTP and is sold as a sleep aid; Wikipedia notes 5-HTP can raise serotonin, which may affect sleep, appetite and body temperature [1].

A 1998 study of NCAA football players over eight weeks of spring training reported greater strength gains with ZMA; it was funded by SNAC Systems, and co-author Victor Conte holds equity in the company [1]. A 2004 study funded by Cytodyne tested a ZMA-containing product and found no significant effects on hormones, strength, endurance or sprint capacity [1].

A 2009 study in 14 healthy, regularly exercising men aged 22 to 33 gave ZMA and measured testosterone. Serum zinc and urinary zinc excretion rose, as did urinary pH and urine flow, while serum total and free testosterone and urinary testosterone metabolites did not change significantly; the authors concluded this applied to men eating a zinc-sufficient diet [2].

Two 2024 trials in the journal Nutrients examined sleep. One tested a single ZMA dose on sleep and next-morning jumps, sprints and a Stroop test in 19 recreationally trained men [3]. The other used a randomized, double-blind crossover design in 16 trained men, comparing ZMA, placebo and a control after two nights of 4-hour sleep, with sleep quality and morning submaximal lifting as outcomes [4]. A clinical review of zinc dosing discusses dietary versus higher pharmacological intakes of zinc, including in male hypogonadism [9].

ZMA is grouped with sleep and testosterone-support supplements in bodybuilding and ascension discussions. On T Nation, one member said it helped them sleep deeper for years [6], another that they fall asleep easier but sleep for less time [7], and another that they had never noticed anything from supplements, ZMA included [10]. A member discussing testosterone said ZMA may raise levels in people who are deficient but does not push testosterone far above normal [11].

lore.intro: ZMA comes up in T Nation training logs and supplement threads, mainly as a pre-bed sleep aid and occasionally as a testosterone support [5][6][7][11].

claims.believers: Several T Nation members report falling asleep more easily or sleeping more deeply after taking it before bed [6][7].
claims.experts: Two 2024 trials examined ZMA and sleep in trained men; their designs were small and short [3][4].

claims.believers: The supplement is marketed for testosterone support, and the 1998 football study reported strength gains [1].
claims.experts: A 2009 trial found no significant change in serum testosterone in men with adequate zinc intake [2]; one forum member notes it may help only those who are deficient [11].

claims.claim: Effects are hard to separate from other changes
claims.believers: A member who restarted ZMA and ashwagandha said progress coincided with other changes and they were unsure which mattered [12].
claims.experts: Funding sources of early ZMA studies have been noted as a point of controversy [1].

card.summary: A zinc, magnesium and B6 night-time supplement sold for sleep and testosterone; the few studies conflict.
card.aka: Zinc magnesium aspartate + B6, Z-Mass PM
card.note: Key supporting study was funded by the trademark holder.

quick.overview:
ZMA is a bundle of zinc, magnesium and vitamin B6, created by BALCO founder Victor Conte and sold to athletes as a pre-bed supplement.

A 1998 company-funded study reported strength gains, while later studies, including an industry-funded one, found no significant hormone or performance effects.
quick.mechanism: The claimed idea is that these minerals support sleep and anabolic hormone processes, with timing before bed intended to improve absorption.
quick.risks: Sold as a dietary supplement. Variants add 5-HTP, which can raise serotonin. Published safety data are not extensively covered in the available sources.

chain: Zinc, magnesium and B6 taken before bed
Reported effects on sleep depth and mineral status
angle.text: Lifters take ZMA in the evening hoping for better sleep and recovery, which they connect to more productive training and muscle gain. Its zinc and magnesium content also addresses intake of two minerals tied to testosterone and sleep in research literature.
